question: Each measles case infects about 15 people, and two vaccine doses protect 97% of children. What percentage must be vaccinated to stop outbreaks?
move: A target for the protected must be divided by how often protection takes.
ask: Which target have I set without dividing by how often the plan really works?
trap: Stopping at 93%, forgetting that some vaccinated children stay unprotected.
hint: Ask what share can stay unprotected if each case must infect fewer than one.
steps: Spread stops when each case infects fewer than one person on average.
So at most 1 in 15 can be susceptible: 1 - 1/15 = 93.3% must be immune.
Only 97% of the vaccinated are immune, so coverage = 93.3 / 0.97.
source: Fine, Eames & Heymann, Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2011
reference: Fine, Eames & Heymann, Herd immunity: a rough guide, Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2011
